title: Omo: Giving Continuing AI-Agent Work a Place to Return To
abstract: arXiv:2611.27107v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI coding agents now keep working while the people who started them are away. Coming back is the hard part: a session list tells you which agent is where, but not what it was asked to do, what it changed, or what to tell it next. We present Omo, which gives each piece of continuing agent work a persistent place to return to. We built the idea twice. Omo Space is an open-source Minecraft mod in which rooms and screens that people build are live terminals on their own machine. Omo Theia brings the same rooms and desks into a customizable IDE, one step away from the editor and the Git patch. Both keep agent sessions running on the host after the view is closed. We describe the two systems, four lessons from building them, and a study designed to test whether returning to a place helps people pick up agent work correctly.

translated_title: Omo：为持续运行的AI智能体工作提供一个可返回的场所
translated_abstract: AI编码智能体现在可以在启动它们的人离开时继续工作，而“回来接手”才是难点：会话列表只能告诉你哪个智能体在哪里，却无法告诉你它被要求做什么、它修改了什么，或者下一步该对它说什么。我们提出了Omo，它为每一项持续进行的智能体工作提供一个可持久返回的场所。我们将这一想法实现了两次：Omo Space是一个开源的Minecraft模组，人们搭建的房间和屏幕就是他们自己机器上的实时终端；Omo Theia则将相同的房间和桌面带入可定制的IDE中，与编辑器和Git补丁仅一步之遥。两者都能在视图关闭后让智能体会话在主机上继续运行。我们描述了这两个系统、构建它们过程中总结出的四点经验教训，以及一项旨在检验“返回到一个场所是否能帮助人们正确接手智能体工作”的研究。
tldr: Omo通过在开源Minecraft模组（Omo Space）和可定制IDE（Omo Theia）中为持续运行的AI智能体工作构建可返回的持久化“场所”（房间、桌面），解决了用户离开后难以了解智能体工作内容并正确接手的问题。
en_tdlr: Omo gives continuing AI-agent work persistent "places to return to" via a Minecraft mod (Omo Space) and a customizable IDE (Omo Theia), helping users correctly pick up agent sessions after being away.
